spec.source_user_request:
# Studio Unit 404: existing HVAC from the record drawing

Recreate the existing HVAC shown for the whole of Studio Unit 404 on sheet M104 in the disposable Level 4 model. Use the loaded architectural background to align the drawing. Work through the unit, inspect the result, repair problems, and return your best completed result with any specific uncertainties or remaining work.

Include the equipment, visible duct routes and fittings, and clearly depicted ceiling devices. Match labeled duct sizes and the drawing's route arrangement. Physically connect duct segments, fittings and equipment where the drawing supports a connection; a drawing that merely looks connected is insufficient. Do not stop after placing equipment or the first duct run.

The sheet notes that water-heater vent duct belongs to the plumbing scope and is shown for coordination. Preserve that distinction. Do not rebuild adjacent units or change the architectural background.

The sheet does not establish all elevations, service identities, airflows, terminal types, or hidden connections. Use defensible assumptions where the drawing permits useful work and state them. Ask a focused question if an ambiguity prevents further progress. Do not invent an exact airflow or device specification merely to complete a field.

Source material: original M104 PDF, whole-sheet image, neighborhood image, detailed Unit 404 image, service-core detail, and scope-note detail. The original sheet governs if a crop omits context.

facts.value: Execute one source-grounded reconstruction stage. The Operator harness normally sends one dependency-ready operation per call, but may send a bounded group of explicitly marked independent high-confidence straight backbones. Each stage runs first with dryRun:true and then once with dryRun:false. Later stages pass hash-ledgered priorActionOutputs so accepted native IDs are never replayed. Each call has its own rollback boundary. Responses echo stageKey and persist created_element_ids, affected_element_ids, and route endpoint IDs; the host ledger binds planned continuation endpoints to those IDs and audits their native connectors before acceptance. In addition to route, family, connection, tag, and circuit creation, the wrapper supports repair-first move, rotate, MEP size/elevation edit, and exact connector repair operations against useful existing elements. Body: {stageKey?,priorActionOutputs?:[{action_key,created_element_ids,affected_element_ids?,route_segment_element_ids?,route_start_element_ids?,route_end_element_ids?,split_main_start_element_ids?,split_main_end_element_ids?}],operations:[{action_key,path,depends_on?,apply_body?,deferred_body?,execution_mode?,provisional_batch_key?,continuation_endpoints?}],dryRun?,verify?,maximumCreatedElements?,targetViewId?,applyTargetViewPhase?,requireAllCreatedElementsVisibleInTargetView?}.
dry-run one repairable existing-conditions stage or bounded provisional backbone batch, apply it once, verify it, and persist created or affected IDs

facts.value: Count placed elements by category and group returned family and type only when itemsComplete is true. A truncated result is not a complete inventory. Selector helper: find element ids by scope (viewId OR sheetNumber) and filters. Supports sheet-region targeting, visible-text search, and bounded document discovery across instance name, family, type, category, and Mark. identityTerms uses exact phrase or at-least-half meaningful-token overlap and returns the matched evidence. physicalElementsOnly excludes view-owned/non-model artifacts; topLevelInstancesOnly excludes nested children. expandIdentityAcronymsInParameters performs a second, category-grounded scan for delimiter-bounded phrase acronyms in string parameters and returns the exact parameter evidence; it never expands without a first-pass physical identity seed. includeGeometry adds each physical result's world-space location, axis-aligned bounding box, orientation, type, level, host, and location-curve length/straightness. Agent projections expose routeCurveCandidates for bounded duct/pipe edit discovery; connector topology must still be verified before mutation. Body: {viewId?,sheetNumber?,includeSheetElements?,includeViewportElements?,sheetRegions?:[{minU,minV,maxU,maxV}],regionPaddingFt?,category?,categories?,typeNameContains?,familyNameContains?,nameContains?,markContains?,textContains?,identityTerms?:string[],physicalElementsOnly?,topLevelInstancesOnly?,expandIdentityAcronymsInParameters?,includeGeometry?,limit?}.
find physical air-terminal instances with world geometry anywhere in this project

facts.value: Create a multi-segment duct, pipe, or electrical conduit route from ordered XYZ or frame-linked points with dry-run, conservative size/elevation fallbacks, explicit user-workset assignment, internal connector attempts, optional fail-closed endpoint joining, and native readback. Set requiredExistingEndpoint=start|end|both with exact expectedExistingStartOwnerId/expectedExistingEndOwnerId for required ends; an explicit endpoint takes precedence over requireExistingEndpointConnections, while true alone requires both ends. Duplicate duct/pipe/conduit type names fail closed; use ductTypeId, pipeTypeId, or conduitTypeId for stable native selection. Duct profiles and dimensions must be valid and compatible before starting a transaction. Native route size, duct shape, and requested workset readback must match when verify=true. Use dryRun:false for authorized creation and true for a requested preview. Body: {kind:duct|pipe|conduit,frameId?,points:[{x?,y?,z?,xPx?,yPx?,xyz?}],viewId?,roomNumber?,levelName?,levelId?,worksetName?,worksetId?,systemType?,ductType?,ductTypeId?,ductShape?:round|rectangular|oval,pipeType?,pipeTypeId?,conduitType?,conduitTypeId?,ductSize?,diameter?,pipeSize?,segmentSizes?:string[],sizePolicy?:explicit_required|use_default_with_warning,elevationPolicy?:explicit_required|resolve_context_default,routingMode?:orthogonal|polyline,connectSegments?,connectToExisting?,requireExistingEndpointConnections?,requiredExistingEndpoint?:start|end|both,expectedExistingStartOwnerId?,expectedExistingEndOwnerId?,externalConnectionToleranceFt?,verify?,dryRun?}.
dry-run a native conduit, pipe, or duct route with three ordered points

Batch place family instances from a spec. Resolve the type by stable familySymbolId or familyName/symbolName. ViewBased symbols require viewId and use Revit's view-owner overload; apply fails closed unless readback proves the exact owner view, target-view collector membership, and a view-specific bounding box. Results include type, owner-view, requested and actual location, collector, and bounding-box evidence. For unhosted non-view-based instances, coordinateMode:absolute_model corrects any family-origin/level offset after creation and fails closed unless LocationPoint readback matches the requested XYZ exactly within tolerance. Non-view-based placement supports default levelName, optional per-instance levelName override, parameters, exact user-workset assignment by worksetName or worksetId, and explicit allowUnhostedWorkPlanePlacement for project-approved unhosted work-plane families. For a linked ceiling, wall or floor, provide hostElementId for its RevitLinkInstance and linkedHostElementId for the exact linked element; linked-face placement checks both native host identities and the projected model-space point after regeneration. Unhosted work-plane placement is not a substitute for a requested ceiling host. Body: {familySymbolId?|familyName?,symbolName?,viewId?,levelName?,worksetId?,worksetName?,allowUnhostedWorkPlanePlacement?,dryRun?,bestEffort?,instances:[{x,y,z,coordinateMode?:absolute_model,levelName?,rotationDegrees?,hostElementId?,linkedHostElementId?,parameters?}]}.

input.reason: Use loaded HRU family and connected native duct route primitives, aligned by M104 grid intersections and checked against architectural background.

facts.value: Get connector identities, origins, sizes, directions, and optional flex duct/pipe control points and tangents for MEP elements. connectorIdBasis is revit_native_connector_id when the active Revit API exposes a durable connector ID; the enumeration_index_with_origin_guard_required fallback must be paired with the returned origin in repair requests. connectedTo preserves all Revit Connector.AllRefs entries; physicalConnectedTo excludes MEPSystem membership objects so isPhysicallyConnected and physicalConnectionCount can be used for actual topology/open-connector checks. Set onlyOpenPhysicalConnectors=true for a compact exhaustive scan that returns summary counts plus only open physical connector rows. Set includeVerificationParameters=true to read System Classification, Reference Level, Width, Height and Diameter in the same native callback as the full connector graph. This mode requires 1-500 unique positive elementIds, includeAllRefs and includeCoordinateSystem, and forbids open-only filtering. It returns verificationParameters with schema revit-operator.duct-verification-parameters/v1; missing fields remain explicit. Body: {elementIds:[...], includeVerificationParameters?, includeAllRefs?, includeCoordinateSystem?, includeFlexGeometry?, onlyOpenPhysicalConnectors?, maxConnectorsPerElement?}.

Type list + family-type maintenance helper. action=list (default) is read-only/low-risk. action=rename_types and action=purge_unused_in_family are high-risk mutation modes and require write approval; dryRun:true makes those modes preview-only but does not downgrade their mutation risk. List supports {category|categories, exactName?, nameContains?, familyNameContains?, includeParameters?, limit?, exportCsv?, outputFolder?, fileName?}. Rename supports {action:"rename_types",familyName,searchPattern,replaceWith?,regexIgnoreCase?,maxEdits?,category|categories?,dryRun?}. Purge supports {action:"purge_unused_in_family",familyName,maxDelete?,category|categories?,dryRun?}.
dry-run rename family types by regex
